name: Agent Skill Induction (ASI) - Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks
venue: COLM 2025 (Second Conference on Language Modeling), accepted (Accept; submission #603; published on OpenReview 07 Jul 2025). Preprint: arXiv:2504.06821 (v1 9 Apr 2025; v2 29 Aug 2025).
authors_affiliation: Zora Zhiruo Wang, Apurva Gandhi, Graham Neubig, Daniel Fried - all Carnegie Mellon University ({zhiruow,apurvag,gneubig,dfried}@cs.cmu.edu). (Zora supported by CMU Presidential Fellowship and Fujitsu Research; Apurva supported by Amazon.)
code_url: https://github.com/zorazrw/agent-skill-induction (linked in the paper footnote and abstract)
task_domain: web - LLM-based web navigation agents. Online, adaptive digital agents that solve natural-language web tasks (e-commerce, social forum, software development, content management, travel) by inducing and reusing programmatic skills. Framed as agentic decision-making / tool-use, not single-shot QA.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent online adaptation in a web browser environment with transition function T(s'|s,a). The agent policy pi_L(.|M,A) consists of an LM backbone L, a memory M, and a skill library A (both M and A are provided as input context to the LM). Given a sequence of NL queries Q={q1,...,qN} specifying tasks (presented in a fixed WebArena order), the agent generates an action trajectory tau=(s0,a0,...,sH) of up to H_max steps, receiving observation o_h (webpage accessibility tree) at each step and emitting an action a_h in A. CRITICAL assumption: NO demonstration trajectories and NO ground-truth rewards are available - the agent learns online purely from test queries (supervision-free), using an LM-based evaluator V_L(e)->0/1 to judge episode correctness. It updates M and A non-parametrically (no LM weight updates) and reuses them across episodes. Skills are induced per-website. Backbone LM is claude-3.5-sonnet for all components (policy, evaluator, induction); implemented in BrowserGym.
what_is_retrieved: skills - reusable programmatic skills represented as executable Python functions (e.g., search_product(name), navigate_to_address_settings()). These verified skill programs are integrated into the agent action space (skill library A) and are directly callable as higher-level actions. (Contrasted with the AWM baseline which retrieves free-text workflow skills stored in memory.)
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / online-induced skill library (procedural memory the agent writes during deployment). The skill library A starts as the fixed WebArena primitive action space (click, fill, etc.) and grows online as the agent induces, verifies, and adds new program-based skills from its own successful episodes. No static external corpus / KB / API docs are retrieved; the store is self-built at test time.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a fixed top-k ranking nor a completeness-recovery objective. ASI does not perform similarity-based top-k retrieval of skills at all; instead, the entire verified skill library A is provided in the LM context (action space) and the LM itself decides which skill to call. The selection objective is the agent autonomously choosing the appropriate higher-level action; quality is governed by execution-based verification at induction time (only skills passing correctness + usage + validity checks enter A), not by a ranking/completeness metric.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: partial (no similarity search; the whole skill library is exposed and the LM selects which skill program to call), Reuse: yes (skill programs are invoked as actions to solve new tasks - 42.5% of cases reuse >=1 skill), Revise: yes (incompatible skills on new websites are updated/extended, e.g., adding a has_popup_window() check, or rewritten), Retain: yes (verified skills are added to the action space A_t U D_called -> A_t+1)]. So approximately Retrieve(partial)/Reuse/Revise/Retain.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed as online adaptive agents, skill induction, program synthesis / tool-making, and non-parametric memory augmentation (building on AWM and TroVE). It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain CBR-like mechanisms under another name (skill induction + verification + reuse + update).
retrieval_unit: skill-or-program - the retrieved/usable unit is an executable Python program function representing a reusable skill (a workflow-routine abstracted as a callable, e.g., search_product(name), open_marketing_reviews(), navigate_and_sort_category(category_id, subcategory_id)). Each wraps multiple primitive actions or prior skills into one higher-level action call. Skills have mediocre complexity (>=2-3 actions, <=5-10 lines) and may include control flow (if-else, for/while loops).
index_source: Online/test-time-induced store. The skill library is grown online from the agent's own successful episodes during the same online run on the target website; it starts only from the fixed primitive action space (no offline skill mining, no pre-collected demonstrations). Skills are induced per-website. Explicitly contrasted with offline skill-mining methods (e.g., SkillWeaver, RL roll-outs) that need supervision/offline compute and may suffer offline-online distribution mismatch.
index_structure_topology: Flat skill library / toolkit: a growing set of callable Python functions provided in the LM context as the agent action space. Skills are organized per-website (some skills are website-tailored with hard-coded link constants; others are versatile). No vector index, no dependency graph, no category hierarchy is used to organize or retrieve skills; the LM reads the full library as context.
retriever_type: LLM-as-selector / generative - there is no separate dense/BM25/learned retriever module. The induced skill programs are placed directly in the agent action space, and the LM backbone (claude-3.5-sonnet) generates actions that call the relevant skill, i.e., skill 'retrieval' is the LM emitting a function call (tool-as-action / generative selection). No embedding similarity search.
retriever_learning_signal: None for any retriever (there is no trained retriever). Skill ENTRY into the action space is gated by execution-based verification (downstream-task-effectiveness): a candidate skill program is admitted only if the verification trajectory passes (1) Correctness (LM-evaluator judges the task solved), (2) Skill Usage (>=1 new skill is called), and (3) Skill Validity (skill-calling actions cause environment changes). So the selection/admission signal is execution + LM-feedback verification, not contrastive similarity or RL-trained retrieval.
query_construction: No explicit query is constructed for skill selection - the agent simply conditions on the current observation/action history (o_0:h, a_0:h-1) plus the in-context skill library and memory, and the LM generates the next action (which may be a skill call). At induction time, the 'query' to the induction module I is a cleaned successful episode e (CoT thoughts simplified from 87.9 to 13.4 tokens/step, error steps removed); for verification a rewritten skill-using trajectory prefix tau_D is constructed by replacing sub-trajectories with skill calls and truncating trailing primitive actions.
query_granularity: step/state-level for skill invocation: at every decision step the LM may emit a skill-call action conditioned on the current observation and history. There is no separate task-level similarity retrieval; skill use is decided per action step within the ReAct-style observe-act loop.
when_to_retrieve: iterative / per-step (agent-initiated) - at each step of the rollout the agent (LM) may choose to call an available skill action; skills become available as soon as they are induced and verified online. Induction/verification of NEW skills is triggered per successful episode (after V_L marks an episode correct).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated, fixed control loop: skill use is triggered whenever the LM decides to emit a skill-call action at a decision step (no confidence/attention/uncertainty/reflection-token gating for using skills). Skill INDUCTION is triggered by an event signal: an episode being predicted correct by the LM-based evaluator V_L (V_L(e)=1) -> the cleaned episode is passed to the induction module; addition to the action space is then triggered by passing the three-way verification check.
reranking: None - no reranking stage of any kind (no cross-encoder, no RRF). Skills are exposed in the action space and selected directly by the LM; admission is by execution verification, not by re-scoring a candidate list.
retrieved_context_refinement: Induction-side refinement rather than post-retrieval reranking: (1) episode cleaning - removing action steps that caused execution errors and LM-summarizing verbose CoT thoughts (87.9 -> 13.4 tokens/step); (2) trajectory rewriting - replacing sub-trajectories with new skill calls to form a skill-using prefix tau_D; (3) trailing-action truncation - removing primitive actions after the last skill call to avoid spurious verification successes; (4) explored but rejected an observe() function for intermediate-state access (caused instability). No distractor filtering / compression of a retrieved candidate set (there is no candidate set).
tool_document_engineering: Skill programs are induced with structured docstrings: the induction module is prompted to include 'Args', 'Returns', and 'Examples' in each function's documentation, plus inline comments, so each skill carries a self-describing docstring used by the LM when deciding to call it. Skill functions are constrained to mediocre complexity (>=2-3 actions, no try-except, no undefined actions). No synthetic-query augmentation or learned tool embeddings (no embedding-based tool retrieval is used).
index_content_separation: N/A - no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content / progressive-disclosure separation; the full skill programs (with docstrings) are loaded directly into the agent action-space context.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Dynamic, live-synchronized skill library that grows during the online run via CRUD-like updates (add verified skills A_t U D_called -> A_t+1; update/extend incompatible skills on new websites). Integration protocol is function-calling / executable-program actions over BrowserGym primitives (click, fill, hover, select_option, etc.); no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP. Skills execute as Python functions composing primitive browser actions.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial - skills can call prior skills (newly induced skills 'wrap primitive actions or prior skills'), so inter-skill composition/dependency is supported in the action space. However there is no explicit dependency-graph modeling, shared-auth tracking, or dependency-aware retrieval/reranking; composition emerges from the LM and the induction module.
how_retrieved_used: skill reuse - induced skill programs are integrated INTO the agent action space (A_t U {d_t} -> A_t+1) and are directly CALLED/EXECUTED as higher-level actions to solve subsequent tasks, composing multiple primitive steps into one. This is explicitly contrasted with AWM, which only adds textual skills to memory (M_t U {d_t} -> M_t+1) for reference/prompt augmentation. ASI's ablation shows that using verified program skills in the action space (40.1 SR) beats placing the same verified programs only in memory (36.4 SR) on the shopping site.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved within an online observe-act (ReAct-style) loop, plus an offline-style induction/verification phase after each successful episode. The agent acts step-by-step; whenever a higher-level skill is available it can be invoked, enabling better/easier planning over fewer, more abstract steps (the paper attributes long-horizon success gains to easier planning with higher-level skills). No MCTS/tree search. The skill induction-verification-reuse cycle runs continuously online.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call within a rollout - skill (tool) calls are interleaved at the level of individual action steps in the agent's trajectory; each step is an action that may be a primitive or a composed skill call. Not per-answer; reasoning CoT precedes each action step.
adaptation_mechanism: execution-feedback-driven revision plus LM-prompted adaptation - retrieved/induced skills are reused largely as-is (called by name), but when a skill is incompatible with a new website, the agent (a) detects the mismatch (from web-design vs skill-implementation discrepancy or from execution error messages in context) and rarely calls the deprecated skill, and (b) updates/extends the prior skill or induces a new skill on the new website (+update setting), e.g., adding a has_popup_window() guard. Skill programs are also rewritten/cleaned during induction.
retrieved_item_representation: executable program-or-skill - the injected/usable unit is an executable Python function (with docstring, Args/Returns/Examples, optional control flow) integrated as a callable action. This is explicitly the central contribution vs AWM's free-text workflow representation in memory.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: procedural skill / reusable workflow - a higher-level abstraction over primitive actions (e.g., search_product composes click+fill+click), at the procedural-skill end of the spectrum, deliberately MORE abstract than raw trajectories and MORE verifiable/composable than free-text workflows (AWM) or single-state guidelines (AutoGuide).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Execution-based verification + LM-evaluator filtering as the primary quality guard: (1) episodes are filtered by an LM evaluator V_L before induction (only predicted-correct episodes are used); (2) only ~15.6% of induction turns produce skills that pass the three-way verification (correctness, skill usage, skill validity) and get added; (3) episode cleaning removes error-causing steps and noisy CoT; (4) trailing-action truncation prevents spurious verification successes; (5) on new websites, execution errors and design discrepancies steer the agent away from incompatible skills and toward updating them. No retriever-side relevance evaluator (no retriever).
memory_type: procedural / skill-library (a growing library of executable program skills in the agent action space). Compared against the AWM baseline's free-text workflow memory; ASI's skills live in the action space A rather than the textual memory M.
write_back: True - verified skill programs are written into the agent skill library (A_t U D_called -> A_t+1) and become callable actions for future tasks; on new websites the agent can also write updated/new skills (+update).
online_growth: True - the skill library grows online during the same deployment run as the agent solves WebArena/scaled-up/cross-website tasks (skills are created from ~7.6% of tasks and reused in 42.5% of cases). There is no separate frozen offline-induction stage; growth happens at test time as queries arrive (in the fixed WebArena order).
write_back_trigger: on-success only, with verification gating: a skill is written to the action space only after (1) the source episode is judged correct by the LM evaluator V_L, AND (2) a rewritten skill-using verification trajectory tau_f passes all three checks - Correctness (LM-evaluator success), Skill Usage (>=1 new skill called), and Skill Validity (skill calls cause environment changes). Failed/unverified inductions are discarded (none added). On new websites, updates are triggered when prior skills are incompatible.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only for storage: only episodes evaluated as correct (and skills passing execution verification) are retained; failed episodes are filtered out and not stored as cases. However, failure signals are used REACTIVELY at use-time: execution error messages from calling an incompatible skill are fed back into context so the agent avoids reusing that skill and instead refines/induces a new one (a corrective, non-stored use of failure). No contrastive failure database is maintained.
memory_evolution_update: append-and-refine: verified skills are appended to the library (append-only growth), and existing skills can be refined-overwrite / extended on new websites (the +update setting rewrites incompatible skills, e.g., adding pop-up handling, or composes new skills referencing prior ones). No forget-prune of skills is described; incompatible skills are simply left unused rather than deleted.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No - skill selection is performed by the (frozen, non-finetuned) LM backbone emitting function-call actions, not by a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. There is no trained retriever, no soft-Q/M-MDP, and no LM weight update (purely non-parametric memory/action-space augmentation). Skill admission is rule-based execution verification.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private skill library (no multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing). The only cross-context transfer studied is the SAME agent transferring its induced skills from sandboxed WebArena websites to real-world counterparts (OneStopMarket->Target, PostMill->Reddit, OpenStreetMap->Google Maps), i.e., cross-website skill generalization by one agent, not sharing across heterogeneous agents/frameworks.
benchmarks: WebArena (812 examples across 5 domains: e-commerce/shopping, social forum/Reddit, software development/GitLab, content management/admin, travel/maps); a curated set of scaled-up long-horizon browsing tasks (multi-subtask, with intermediate checkpoints, ~10 examples per website across shopping/admin/Reddit/GitLab/maps); and cross-website real-world tasks (10 information-seeking queries each on Target, Reddit, Google Maps, mapped from OneStopMarket/PostMill/OpenStreetMap).
benchmark_family: web (WebArena and WebArena-derived scaled-up + real-world cross-website tasks). Sandbox-to-real transfer pairs cover shopping (OneStopMarket->Target), online forum (PostMill->Reddit), and travel/maps (OpenStreetMap->Google Maps).
baselines: Vanilla static agent (Claude/claude-3.5-sonnet + BrowserGym, no adaptation; also a GPT/gpt-4o vanilla in Table 1) and AWM (Agent Workflow Memory, Wang et al. 2024b), the prior top-performing online adaptive web agent that induces free-text workflow skills into memory (run with both gpt-4o and, for fair comparison, claude-3.5-sonnet + episode cleaning). Ablation conditions: (unverified,text in memory), (verified,program in memory), (verified,text in memory), (verified,program as actions = ASI). Rebuttal-added baseline: trajectory-as-prompt (previous episodes directly in context) = 35.6 SR / 6.3 steps. Positioned against (not run) SkillWeaver (concurrent, offline), TroVE, AutoGuide, AutoManual, Voyager, Synapse.
key_metrics: Success rate (SR; WebArena program-based binary 0/1 evaluator, averaged over examples; scaled-up uses percentage of intermediate checkpoints achieved); number of steps (#Steps, efficiency, lower is better); LLM input/output token counts (efficiency, from rebuttal); statistical significance (paired t-test |t|>2, p<0.05).
headline_result: On WebArena with claude-3.5-sonnet, ASI reaches 40.4% overall SR, surpassing the static vanilla agent by 23.5% relative (32.7 -> 40.4) and the AWM text-skill agent by 11.3% relative (36.3 -> 40.4), while using fewer steps (5.0 vs 5.6 vanilla / 5.9 AWM, i.e., 15.3% / 10.6% fewer). The ASI vs AWM SR gain is statistically significant (paired t-test t=-2.21, p=0.027). In scaled-up long-horizon tasks ASI outperforms vanilla and AWM by 38.9% and 20.7% on average and is markedly more efficient (e.g., shopping 100.0% SR / 16.3 steps vs AWM 68.3% / 21.5; up to 85.2% horizon reduction in the multi-address case study).
ablations: (1) Verification + format ablation on the shopping site (Table 3): Add-to-Memory (unverified,text)=32.6 -> (verified,program)=36.4 (+4.2 from execution-verified induction) -> (verified,text)=39.0 (+2.6, text suits memory better); Add-as-Actions (verified,program)=ASI=40.1 (program format suits action space). So both verification quality AND action-space integration drive the gain. (2) Episode-cleaning ablation (rebuttal): without cleaning AWM=35.5, ASI=38.5 (cleaning adds +0.8/+1.9; not necessary, still beats vanilla). (3) Trajectory-as-prompt baseline (rebuttal): 35.6 SR / 6.3 steps, 4.8 below ASI and 26% more steps. (4) Skill induction/reuse analysis (Table 8): skills created from 7.6% of tasks, reused in 42.5% of cases (e.g., shopping 21 attempted / 8 successful / 96 reuse). (5) Token-efficiency (rebuttal): ASI cuts input tokens 8.0% (301190->277208) and output tokens 12.9% (761->663) vs vanilla. (6) Significance testing on scaled-up and cross-web tasks (Tables 17-18). (7) Cross-website +update ablation (Table 6).
evaluation_decoupling: No - the paper reports end-to-end task success rate and efficiency (steps, tokens) but does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) decoupled from task performance (there is no top-k retrieval to evaluate). The closest decoupled signals are skill induction/reuse rates (attempted/successful/reuse counts) and the ~15.6% verification pass rate, which are induction-quality diagnostics rather than retrieval-quality metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and process: outcome = success rate (with checkpoint-level partial credit on scaled-up tasks, giving intermediate-progress granularity); process/efficiency = number of steps and input/output token counts (trajectory quality / adherence to the optimal route), induction and reuse frequencies, and qualitative case studies of trajectory quality. WebArena's program-based evaluator scores functional correctness of the trajectory.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency story: ASI reduces steps by 10.7-15.3% on general WebArena and by 4.0-8.4% (AWM) / 6.6-14.6 steps (vanilla) on scaled-up tasks; up to 85.2% horizon reduction in the multi-address case. Token efficiency (rebuttal): -8.0% input tokens, -12.9% output tokens vs vanilla. Induction adds online compute (episode cleaning, induction LM calls, and a verification re-solve per candidate skill), and skills are created from only 7.6% of tasks; but ASI does NOT require offline exploration/supervision (unlike SkillWeaver/RL methods). Caveat (Reviewer nthk): step counts hide that the number of underlying environment interactions is unchanged when a skill bundles atomic actions; token counts are the cleaner efficiency metric. [uncertain on absolute wall-clock/dollar cost]
context_budget_and_selection_count: No fixed top-k selection - the entire verified skill library is exposed in the agent's action-space context and the LM selects which skill to call. Skill complexity is bounded (>=2-3 actions, <=5-10 lines, no try-except) to keep the library compact and reusable. Episode cleaning shrinks induction-input CoT from 87.9 to 13.4 tokens/step. No explicit numeric token budget cap is stated for the action space. [uncertain on exact prompt token budget]
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses the existing WebArena benchmark (812 examples, 5 domains, program-based 0/1 verifier). Two author-curated test sets: scaled-up long-horizon tasks (~10 examples per website over shopping/admin/Reddit/GitLab/maps, each created by extending WebArena tasks to multi-item/multi-subtask requests, scored by manually-defined intermediate checkpoints) and cross-website real-world tasks (10 information-seeking, non-risky queries per site on Target/Reddit/Google Maps). Answer verifiability: WebArena via program-based evaluator; curated tasks via checkpoint-based human-defined scoring. [uncertain on exact scaled-up/cross-web total counts beyond ~10 per website]
builds_on: AWM - Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2024b): the direct predecessor that induces and reuses workflows from online experiences via non-parametric memory augmentation; ASI changes the skill representation from free-text-in-memory to verifiable-executable-program-in-action-space. Also builds on TroVE (Wang et al. 2024a, inducing verifiable/efficient toolboxes for programmatic tasks), program-synthesis/library-learning (DreamCoder, LILO, LLMs-as-Tool-Makers), ReAct-style observe-act agents, BrowserGym (Chezelles et al. 2024) and WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024a), and embodied skill-as-program work (Voyager, Code-as-Policies).
contrasts_with: AWM (free-text, non-executable, unverifiable skills in memory) - the primary contrast; AutoGuide (single-state textual guidelines) and CLIN (causal abstractions); offline skill-mining methods such as SkillWeaver (concurrent; offline API creation needing supervision and offline compute, with offline-online mismatch), RL-rollout web-skill methods (WebRL, Agent Q, PAE), and SFT/contrastive self-improvement (NNetscape Navigator, Patel et al.). Also contrasts step-counting efficiency with token-based efficiency raised in review.
lineage: Group A/experiential-memory agent self-improvement lineage, on the procedural-skill / programmatic-tool branch. Lineage: ReAct -> non-parametric experiential memory (Reflexion, Synapse, ExpeL) and workflow induction (AWM) -> programmatic, execution-verified skill induction integrated into the action space (ASI), as the executable-program successor to text-workflow-memory approaches; sibling to TroVE (programmatic toolboxes) and Voyager (skill library) and concurrent with SkillWeaver (offline API induction).
